title: eleusine coracana var. stricta
intro: Eleusine coracana var. stricta, commonly known as finger millet, is a type of millet plant native to Africa and Asia, known for its small, round seeds and drought-resistant properties. Finger millet is rich in nutrients and has been associated with various health benefits, including improved digestion, reduced inflammation, and enhanced immune function, due to its high content of dietary fiber, vitamins, and minerals. The therapeutic actions of finger millet include anti-diabetic, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant properties, which are attributed to its bioactive constituents, such as phenolic compounds, flavonoids, and saponins. The bioactive constituents of finger millet include ferulic acid, quercetin, and kaempferol, which have been shown to exhibit antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial activities.
